newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian fund managers to give up directorships.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian fund managers to give up directorships.

text.p: Egyptian stock exchange authorities have told fund managers to give up directorships of any listed companies, brokers and fund managers said on Thursday.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) gave the order as part of a campaign against suspected insider trading and price manipulation by mutual fund managers, they said.

The order comes into effect immediately but in practice it could take some weeks to find alternative directors. The CMA has proposed that the banks which sponsor the mutual funds recommend alternative candidates.
The reaction to the order was mixed among fund managers, even among those who hold such directorships.

"I'm against it. It's contrary to the trend in the rest of the world, where institutional and other funds are more and more involved as directors of companies," said a senior executive at a big Cairo brokerage. He declined to be named.

"The directors should be those who have an interest in maximising the company's value to the shareholders. If it's to stop insider trading, it's cosmetic. If insider trading does take place, one should come down hard," he added.
But another director-manager said he believed insider trading had taken place and the CMA was right to act.
"It's a pity but it's natural that the CMA should tell them to resign. But the real problem is the level of disclosure (of company information)," he said.
The CMA decreed last March that all listed companies should release quarterly results within one month of the end of the period but most companies have ignored this with impunity.
In practice information about the performance of the most active companies circulates among brokers well before the companies publish it or deliver it to the CMA.
Another big mutual fund manager, one who holds no directorships, said he approved of the CMA decree because the funds were often short-term players in the markets.
"It makes sense. They might take a seat on the board on the basis of their holding today and liquidate tomorrow," he said.
CMA officials were not available to comment on the decree.
